The Hershey Company
CALIFORNIA TRANSPARENCY IN SUPPLY CHAINS ACT

The Hershey Company, together with its subsidiaries, recognizes the importance of the California Transparency in Supply Chains Act of 2010, which is designed to increase the amount of information manufacturers and retailers make available regarding their efforts to address issues related to slavery and human trafficking in their supply chains. We endeavor to model good business practices by striving to ensure our supply chains are responsibly managed.

Hershey has a history of operating with high ethical standards and integrity. The manner in which our employees and vendors manage social, environmental, and economic impacts is critical to our long-term business success.

We have established a Supplier Code of Conduct that sets forth Hershey’s standards and expectations for suppliers with respect to corporate and social responsibility. We require our suppliers to acknowledge their understanding of and adhere to our Supplier Code of Conduct, which serves as a key governing component of our business relationship with these third parties.

As outlined in the Supplier Code of Conduct, our goal is to work with our suppliers to assure compliance with the following requirements:

Legal and Compliance

Suppliers must comply with all applicable laws and regulations in their country of operation.

Social and Working Conditions

Forced Labor: Suppliers must not utilize or benefit in any way from forced or compulsory labor nor utilize factories or subcontractors that force unpaid labor.

Child Labor: Hershey is committed to the elimination from its supply chain of the worst forms of child labor, as defined by the International Labor Organization (ILO) Convention 138 and 182. We expect our suppliers to support and participate in industry efforts aimed at the elimination of such practices, wherever they exist in the supply chain.

Working Hours and Wages: Suppliers should provide wages at least equal to the applicable legal minimum wage and any associated statutory benefits, and working hours should reflect applicable legal norms, which includes supplier compliance with applicable laws regarding working and overtime hours.

Freedom of Association: Consistent with local regulations, employees’ right to freedom of association should be respected by suppliers, including that employee relationships are voluntary in nature.

Non-Discrimination: Supplier hiring and employment decisions should be made solely on the basis of skill, ability and performance by the workers, and discrimination is not permitted on the basis of race, religion, gender, political opinion, national extraction, or social origin.

Health and Safety: Suppliers must provide employees with safe and health working environments and practices must comply with all relevant local and national laws, codes, and regulations.

Supplier Verification and Audits

Hershey reserves the right to monitor, review and verify supplier compliance with the principles set forth in the Supplier Code of Conduct, either through third-party certifications or a responsible sourcing audit, which may be performed by a third party. In the event the Company becomes aware of non-compliance, we maintain the right to set forth corrective actions and/or terminate our business relationship with the supplier.

Hershey requires key suppliers to undergo the Sedex Members Ethical Trade Audit (SMETA), developed by the Associate Auditor Group of the Sustainable Ethical Data Exchange. SMETA is a prescriptive audit procedure that is a compilation of effective ethical audit techniques.

In 2013, Hershey used third-party auditors to complete social assessments on 25 percent of its external suppliers (based on spend). In 2014, Hershey used third-party auditors to begin assessing an additional 25 percent of its external suppliers (based on spend).

Code of Ethical Business Conduct

Hershey has committed to operating with the highest of ethical standards. This commitment dates to the founding of our company and has earned Hershey a reputation for fairness and honesty throughout the world.

The Company’s Code of Ethical Business Conduct (Code of Conduct) sets forth the standards by which we conduct our operations and establishes a clear expectation that the standards be followed in all job-related activities, regardless of business pressure. It further memorializes our commitment to consumers by maintaining the trust consumers place in our brands, providing the best products in the market and adhering to honest marketing practices.

Employee Training

Our Code of Conduct is distributed to all Hershey employees and is supplemented by targeted training and communications addressing the values set forth within it. Every year employees must complete training modules or acknowledge the standards, guidelines and practices set for in our Code of Conduct. Non-compliance with the Code of Conduct and related Company policies may subject employees to discipline, up to and including termination.

answer:
computer_science.completion: When the page table is in main memory, a single access requires two main memory accesses: the first access is to retrieve the page table and obtain the physical address of the page where the required data is located; the second access is to fetch the data using this physical address. You buy one share of stock at a price of $25. One year later, you receive a dividend of $2 and sell the stock at a price of $33. What is your holding-period return ____?
options:
A.45$\%$
B.50$\%$
C.4$\%$
D.40$\%$
answer:
financial.completion:
D.40$\%$
explanation:
1. Holding-period return = (selling price - purchase price + dividend) / purchase price. Substitute the values into the formula to calculate: the holding-period return equals (33-25+2)/25=10/25=0.4, i.e., 40$\%$.

Accounting measurement is a basic feature of financial accounting, and it occupies an important position in the theory and methods of financial accounting. Which of the following statements about accounting measurement attributes is incorrect? ____
options:
A.Historical cost reflects the past value of an asset.
B.Replacement cost is the current cost of acquiring an identical or similar asset.
C.Present value is the cash or other equivalent that needs to be paid currently to acquire an asset.
D.Fair value refers to the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.
answer:
financial.completion:
C.Present value is the cash or other equivalent that needs to be paid currently to acquire an asset.
explanation:
1. Present value refers to the amount obtained by discounting future net cash flows at an appropriate discount rate; it is a measurement attribute that takes into account factors such as the time value of money.

question: Linear Technology’s disclosure states that it maintains internal accountability standards and procedures for employees or contractors failing to meet slavery-and-trafficking standards. It also identifies inaccurate supplier self-certifications or noncompliance as material breaches that may result in product rejection or relationship termination. The company elects to reject goods originally costing $100,000 after an inaccurate self-certification. Identical compliant replacements are delivered immediately under either quote: $120,000 payable today or $132,000 payable in one year. At a 10% annual discount rate, which assessment correctly addresses the accountability disclosure, compares replacement payments in today’s dollars, and distinguishes the original price from current replacement cost? Exclude refunds and all other cash flows.

options.A: Yes; rejection is permitted, not required. The $100,000 is historical cost and $120,000 is current replacement cost. Choose payment today because it costs $12,000 less than deferred payment.
options.B: Yes; rejection is permitted, not required. Historical cost measures past value, replacement cost measures current acquisition cost, and present value discounts future payments; these definitions alone leave the quotes unranked.
options.C: Yes; rejection is permitted, not required. The $100,000 is historical cost; current replacement cost is $120,000. Both quotes have a present value of $120,000, so neither is cheaper on the stated basis.
options.D: Yes; rejection is permitted, not required. Both quotes have a present value of $120,000, but the material breach automatically recovers the $100,000 historical cost, making either replacement expenditure $20,000.

explanation: The disclosure expressly states that internal accountability standards and procedures exist and identifies consequences for inaccurate self-certifications or noncompliance. Its use of 'may' makes rejection discretionary; the company’s stipulated election creates the replacement decision. The original $100,000 is historical cost, not the current cost of acquiring replacements. The immediate quote establishes a current replacement cost of $120,000. The deferred payment has present value $132,000 / 1.10 = $120,000, so the quotes are equivalent when only replacement payments are compared.

distractor_analysis.reason: It correctly assesses the disclosure and distinguishes historical from replacement cost, but compares nominal payments at different dates without discounting. The $12,000 nominal difference does not make immediate payment cheaper in present-value terms.

It supplies a correct legal assessment and separate financial definitions but never applies the given amounts and discount rate to the purchasing decision. The available information establishes present-value equivalence.

It correctly discounts the replacement quotes but incorrectly turns a material-breach provision into an automatic financial recovery. The disclosure establishes no such recovery, and deducting it would also violate the instruction to exclude refunds and other cash flows.

answer:
computer_science.completion: The datagram length is 4000B, with a payload of 4000-20=3980B. The maximum payload that the network can transmit is 1500-20=1480B, so it should be divided into 3 shorter fragments, with data field lengths of 1480, 1480, and 1020B, respectively. The unit for the fragment offset field is 8B, 1480/8=185, (1480x2)/8=370, so the values for the fragment offset field are 0, 185, and 370, respectively. When MF=1, it indicates that there are more fragments to follow; when MF=0, it indicates that there are no more fragments, so the values for the MF field are 1, 1, and 0, respectively.

question: A service states: “The Services conduct research on our users demographics, interests and behavior based on the information we collect. We do this to better understand and serve our users, and to improve our products and services.” Its survey asks tablet users how often they would watch video advertisements for free streaming: Never 31.3%, Rarely 24.3%, Often 13.5%, Always 30.9%. Two projects would use these survey data: 1. Internal research into an ad-supported free-streaming pilot to improve the service. 2. Selling the survey data to advertisers solely for resale revenue. Select a project only if its purpose is described by the clause and at least 40% of respondents who did not answer Never answered Always. Does the clause describe how and why information is used, what is that conditional probability, and which project meets both criteria? Assess disclosed purpose, not legal authorization.

options.A: Yes; approximately 45%; select both projects because the numerical threshold is met.
options.B: Yes; approximately 45%; select only project 1, whose service-improvement research purpose is described.
options.C: Yes; approximately 45%; report the clause's research purpose and the survey result separately, without selecting a project.
options.D: Yes; approximately 45%; select both projects because willingness to watch ads grants permission for data resale, bringing it within the disclosed purpose.

explanation: The clause explains how collected information is used—research into user demographics, interests, and behavior—and why: understanding and serving users and improving services. Among respondents who did not answer Never, the probability of Always is 30.9/(100 − 31.3) = 30.9/68.7 ≈ 0.45, exceeding 40%. Project 1 also matches the stated research and service-improvement purpose. Resale solely for revenue is not a purpose described by this clause, so project 2 fails that criterion. This comparison does not establish legal authorization.

distractor_analysis.reason: It correctly applies the numerical screen but ignores the requirement that each project's purpose match the clause. Resale solely for revenue is not described.
It recognizes the clause's purpose and calculates the probability correctly, but leaves them disconnected rather than applying both criteria to select project 1.

It incorrectly converts willingness to watch advertisements into permission to sell survey information. The survey result neither changes the clause's stated purpose nor establishes legal authorization.

question: A service's clause states: “To Better Understand Our Readers and Users. The Services conduct research on our users demographics, interests and behavior based on the information we collect. We do this to better understand and serve our users, and to improve our products and services.” The service collects a survey asking tablet users how often they would watch video advertisements to access streaming content for free: Never 31.3%, Rarely 24.3%, Often 13.5%, Always 30.9%. Two proposed projects use these data: (1) internal research into an ad-supported free-streaming pilot to improve the service; (2) selling the survey data to advertisers solely for resale revenue. Select a project only if its purpose is described by the clause and at least 40% of respondents who did not answer Never answered Always. Does the clause describe how and why collected information is used, what is P(Always | not Never), and which project(s) meet both criteria? Assess disclosed purpose, not legal authorization.

options.A: Yes; approximately 0.45; select both projects because the survey passes the numerical screen.
options.B: Yes; approximately 0.45; the clause describes service-improvement research, but leave project selection unresolved.
options.C: Yes; approximately 0.45; select project 1 only, without inferring legal authorization.
options.D: Yes; approximately 0.45; select both projects because willingness to watch ads makes data resale a disclosed purpose.

explanation: The clause describes using collected information for research into users' demographics, interests, and behavior to understand users and improve services. Among respondents who did not answer Never, the Always proportion is 30.9/(100 − 31.3) = 30.9/68.7 ≈ 0.45, exceeding 40%. Project 1 also matches the disclosed service-improvement research purpose. Project 2's sole purpose of resale revenue is not described by this clause. This purpose comparison does not establish legal authorization.
